chunks: Credit Card Dispute Resolution Policy

Customers may dispute unauthorized transactions, billing errors, or fraudulent charges on their credit card account within 60 days of the statement date. To initiate a dispute, customers should contact support with their account details and a description of the disputed transaction.

Once a dispute is filed, the bank will investigate within 10 business days. During this period, the disputed amount may be temporarily credited back to the customer's account pending investigation. If fraud is confirmed, the charge is permanently reversed and the card is reissued with a new number
. If the dispute is found invalid, the temporary credit is reversed and the customer is notified with supporting evidence.

Customers experiencing double charges or failed transactions where funds were deducted should report immediately, as these are typically resolved faster (within 3-5 business days) since they involve clear transaction records
. Repeated unauthorized charges may indicate a compromised card, and the bank recommends immediate card freezing in such cases.
Credit Reporting Error Correction Policy

Customers who identify inaccurate information on their credit report (incorrect account status, wrong payment history, accounts that do not belong to them) can file a dispute with the credit reporting department
. Disputes must include supporting documentation where available (payment receipts, account statements).

Upon receiving a dispute, the bank is required to investigate and respond within 30 days as per standard credit reporting regulations. If an error is confirmed, the correction is submitted to all major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion) within 5 business days of confirmation.

Cases involving identity theft or accounts fraudulently opened in a customer's name are treated as high priority and are escalated to the fraud investigation team immediately. Customers should also be advised to place a fraud alert on their credit file during the investigation period
. Repeated reporting errors on the same account may warrant a full account audit.
Debt Collection Practices and Customer Rights Policy
The bank engages in debt collection only for legitimately owed amounts and follows fair debt collection practices
. Customers have the right to request written validation of any debt within 30 days of first contact, including the amount owed, the original creditor, and their right to dispute the debt.

Customers who believe they are being contacted about a debt in error, or who dispute the validity of a debt, should immediately request this in writing. All collection activity must pause until the debt is verified and a response is provided to the customer.

Customers facing financial hardship may request a payment plan or settlement negotiation. Harassment, repeated calls outside permitted hours, or threats are strictly against policy — such complaints are escalated to compliance review immediately
. Debt collection complaints combined with credit reporting disputes should be handled jointly, as they are often related to the same underlying account issue.

Mortgage and Loan Complaint Resolution Policy

Customers experiencing issues with mortgage servicing (incorrect payment application, escrow errors, loan modification requests, foreclosure concerns) should contact the loan servicing department with their loan number and a description of the issue.
For payment application errors, the bank will review the last 12 months of payment history and correct any misapplied payments within 10 business days
. Escrow discrepancies (property tax or insurance shortfalls/overages) are reviewed annually but can be escalated for immediate review if the customer disputes the calculation.
Customers facing financial hardship and at risk of missed payments should be directed toward loan modification or forbearance programs before any escalation to collections or foreclosure proceedings
. Complaints involving imminent foreclosure are treated as urgent and routed directly to the loss mitigation team within 24 hours.
Retail Banking Services Policy
This policy covers day-to-day banking issues including account access, ATM/debit card problems, online/mobile banking errors, and branch service complaints
. Customers unable to access their account online should first verify credentials; persistent access issues after verification should be escalated to technical support.
For ATM or debit card transaction errors (failed withdrawals where funds were deducted, double debits), the bank will investigate and refund confirmed errors within 5 business days
. Lost or stolen cards should be reported immediately for blocking, with a replacement card issued within 3-5 business days.
Complaints regarding branch service quality or staff conduct are forwarded to branch management for review and do not typically require financial remediation unless a direct financial error occurred
. Account linking issues with third-party apps are common and usually resolved by re-authenticating credentials or checking for temporary service outages.
General Complaint Escalation Policy

All customer complaints are first assessed for sentiment and category. Complaints expressing significant distress, financial harm, or involving fraud, identity theft, or legal/regulatory concerns are automatically escalated to a human agent for priority handling, regardless of category.

Standard complaints are addressed through automated resolution where a clear policy applies (e.g., standard refund timelines, known error corrections). If a complaint does not clearly match an existing policy, or if the customer explicitly requests to speak with a representative, it is escalated.

Complaints involving repeated unresolved issues (the same customer contacting multiple times about the same issue) are automatically flagged for priority review, as repeated contact indicates the initial resolution was inadequate
. All escalated complaints receive a response acknowledgment within 24 hours and a target resolution timeline communicated to the customer.
